title: Upload an XP game to Itch.io?

posts.author: Jotari
posts.body: Can you upload RPG Maker XP games to Itch.io? I see support for other RPG Maker games to do so, but not XP. Can it be done, and if so, how?

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
You can upload any files to itch, so yes.
For making it playable in browser without downloading, I don't think there's a way to do that with pre-MV makers.

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body:
Yes, you can upload on itch.io, but it can't be playable in the browser on itch.io's page.
Only MV and MZ can do that.

There is a VX Ace to MV converter, but I'm not aware of anything for XP. You could export the maps as images and use those as parallaxes, but otherwise you'd need to remake them.
MV vs MZ is a topic of much debate here, you can find plenty of past discussions on the forums. I personally prefer MV due to a more pleasant plugin ecosystem, but the right choice will depend on what your priorities are.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Seconding Slim's XP to MZ recommendation, I
hated
VXA/MV mapping. If you're used to XP's really controllable layers, you will be extremely frustrated by the lack of control MV gives you.
XP maps cannot be ported. You can reuse your graphics in MZ, though. 32px tiles can be used in MZ natively (just choose the setting in the database) but you'll need to adjust how tilesets are formatted. XP wants 256 wide and they can be however long you want them to be, whereas MZ wants four 512px squares for 32px graphics. Autotiles are also shaped differently between the two. MV only supports 48px graphics.
Making tall sprites work in MZ (like the XP RTP ones) takes some plugin wizardry that I haven't yet tried to sort out, but it can definitely be done.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
None of the RPG Makers have a spellcheck, unfortunately xD
XP in particular has a quirk where the text box is sized for four lines, but for some reason it only allows input to three--you can get around that by using "Batch Text Entry" instead of "Show Text" in your events. Trihan has a script to allow text formatting (bold, italic, size, etc) that's free to use and very simple!
Trilobytes Message System XP
But between MV/Z, I will continue to wholeheartedly recommend MZ. It's well worth the price.

Vanilla MZ beats vanilla MV out of the water. Yes, years ago when MZ was new the map editor, the new battle systems and the animations were the biggest differences (although it also had a lot of smaller QoL stuff like movement preview, name window built in, plugin commands drop down list, changing the resolution, performance improvement etc.).
MZ has gotten so many new features through the years: being able to change tile size, being able to do both Effekseer animations and the old RM animations, being able to test only parts of your event, being able to use subfolders, etc. I also don't think the plugin difference is that big anymore between the two. (At least I've never had an issue finding what I needed.)
Anyway from my own personal experience, the jump from XP to MZ is a lot easier than the jump from XP to MV.

Yanfly suite by itself is far better than VisuStella since it's far cheaper, not bloated with unnecessary features, and not code obfuscated, so conflicts can be addressed.
There is still a significant difference in plugins. For example, most of SRD, Galv, and Moghunter only have MV versions. I haven't found an MZ equivalent of Graphical Design Mode, ZE free jump, Mighty Mouse, or a diagonal pathfinding plugin outside of Chaucer's paid collsion plugin. Even if a plugin for a feature for MZ exists, there will be multiple options for MV you can choose from in case one conflicts with your other plugins.
